how: An initial proposer supplies a recognizable mark and location for others to answer.
Repeated calls gather builders for successive pictures and for holding existing work.
A participant explains the canvas as a digital graffiti wall to someone asking what it is.
A stated shortage of workers and an approaching freeze prompt renewed recruitment.
A proposed mark and location give the build invitation an object that helpers can answer.
Build calls are followed by reports of placing and requests for actionable pictures.
A helper accepts a build call with a bare yes.
A bare No followed by shut limits the claim that declining necessarily supplies a reason without negating the observed bare acceptance.
Builders choose forms and revise their size and alignment to fit adjacent pieces.
Builders report progress but also correct apparent placement as a registration bug.
Coordinates, first-pixel instructions, templates and shading corrections guide where helpers place.
A template can require further moving rather than demonstrate an agreed design or completed compliance.
Organizers move planning into chat and return instructions to the public thread.
Chat-based planning needs reachable invitations and public tasks for helpers who remain outside chat.
A failed invitation is replaced so that the advertised coordination venue remains reachable.
Invitations establish routing into chat but not universal access or visibility into its decisions.
Instructions allocate defense to those not building the next picture and supply a task for helpers outside chat.
The aggregate rarity claim cannot erase local task allocation or convert host posting sanctions into canvas government.
Failed registration and restarting do not establish machines, extra accounts or placement beyond the timer.
The reported registration bug supplies no evidence of scripts or spare accounts used for construction.
Upkeep strain is visible but no machine-hands response is observed, leaving the proposed mechanism untestable locally.
Builders defend an existing mark while others extend the display and spend repeated placements holding off vandals.
An already placed Brand becomes a defense task while other builders make the next picture.
Participants distinguish hostile red-bombing from their own intentional teardown and identify repair based on missing notice.
Repair needs an up-to-date target because fixing planned erasure can undo the organizers' relocation.
Repeated destruction prompts abandoning the old Brand and discussing another location.
Relocation also happens to keep allied pieces together or avoid an approaching taskbar before completed destruction.
Shortage is explicitly answered with recruitment while the stated moving rationales are destruction, cooperative adjacency and preventive avoidance.
Moving includes telling helpers to stop repairing the abandoned or intentionally erased version.
A helper's explanation of obsolete repair prompts a request to raise the visibility of the relocation notice.
Neighbours propose a truce and report a space-sharing deal that keeps related pieces together.
An outside room's offer of help is welcomed into the coordination chat.
Builders describe joint artwork and shared-window coordination with neighbouring communities.
A taskbar threat is answered with an explicit coalition plan to route the bar beneath the shared artwork.
A participant invokes prior coordination and lack of interference when asking others not to sabotage a neighbouring logo.
Invoking a coordinated border supports an appeal for restraint but does not establish compliance by all helpers.
Upkeep and truce talk are present without an explicit local account that erosion caused this negotiation.
Help is offered because the neighbour's work looks good rather than explicitly because the recipient has run short of hands.
Offers of help and border requests do not show that border negotiation produced an exchange of delivered assistance.
Offering to contact a territorial host establishes a proposed envoy but not completed representation or an answered request.
Expected permission for red art is hearsay and the proposed contact has no visible host ruling.
Questioning abandonment and repairing without notice do not state that an agreement lacks authority to bind members.
A deal receives a logistical question rather than a visible denial of anyone's right to commit the room.
A vandalism report receives a joke about a familiar fictional antagonist.
The fictional-antagonist joke does not identify a pre-existing quarrel with a real canvas opponent.
Lore attached to vandalism is not itself an inherited real rivalry naming a target in an attack turn.
Believable fake hiatus, spoiler and season announcements are revealed or challenged as April Fools misdirections.
April Fools also licenses making and sharing fan-work variants rather than only deceptive announcements or takeovers.
A wish for a subreddit takeover and a remembered refusal cannot be treated as an enacted takeover.
A surviving date announcement with a removed body does not reveal the conduct that body contained.
The host funnels canvas talk into one permitted topic or chat and threatens sanctions for additional topics.
The moderator explicitly gives an influx of canvas topics as the reason to restrict further posting.
Participants celebrate completion, thank builders and claim the artwork as a collective accomplishment.
Reported completed Brands become objects of public thanks and pride.
A completion celebration can be provisional and coexist with an explicit statement that the work is not over.
Celebration is followed by invitations to a next project on the same canvas rather than only a terminal memorial stage.
An explicit not-over reply and a defense instruction qualify the celebration of the existing Brand.
An edited closing report records the result while explicitly preserving the unfinished Behelit move.
Celebration and a final-result report share an edited item without independent evidence that celebration prompted recording.
Taking up another picture on the same canvas does not establish preserving the effort beyond this event.
A final report is visible but no record-led continuation beyond the canvas is supplied.
Late lore and placement complaints do not contest a cleaned-up canvas copy or a historical account.
A neighbour reports encroachment by the room's artwork without establishing an organized attack intention.
A complaint about running over another work supports reported damage but not a verified deliberate raid.
A poorly received joke elsewhere and a local logo rebuke do not demonstrate a sustained interroom verbal contest.
Build calls and a later encroachment complaint do not show recruits being turned toward an attack.
A reasoned restraint plea is visible but not as a response to a visible attack call.
The reported deal is not presented as an answer to an attack call.
Damage complaints and isolated rebukes do not show an attack generating an interroom taunting sequence.
